title: Pi-hole
description: The Pi-hole pair, pihole-01 and pihole-02, and their keepalived VIP: which instance serves clients (inferred from query rate; keepalived exports no metrics), each instance's probes, queries, blocking, cache and gravity, the top domains, and the top clients named from NetBox. pihole-exporter (job="pihole") and the blackbox DNS probes. Replaces the vendored Pi-hole Exporter (grafana.com 10176). docs/design/dns-chain.md, docs/design/host-monitoring.md.

list.name: client
list.label: Client
list.description: The selected instances' ten top clients, for the NetBox lookup in Top clients.

panels.title: Serving clients
panels.description: The instance answering most queries right now, which is the one holding the VIP: every client asks the VIP, and the other instance sees only probes and nebula-sync. Inferred from query rate among instances whose dns_lookup probe passes (the exporter repeats a dead instance's last rate), not read from keepalived, which exports no metrics.

panels.title: VIP answering
panels.description: The blackbox dns_lookup probe through the VIP: a public name resolved the way every client resolves it.

panels.title: Instances answering
panels.description: Selected instances whose own dns_lookup probe passed. probe_success, not pihole_status, says an instance is down: the exporter repeats its last reading when one API stops answering.

targets.expr: count(probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_lookup", instance=~"pihole-0.*", instance=~"$instance"} == 1) or vector(0)

panels.title: Exporter
panels.description: Whether the gateway's scrape of pihole-exporter succeeds. Down means every panel below is frozen at its last value, not that Pi-hole is down.

panels.title: Queries today
panels.description: DNS queries the selected instances answered since midnight.

panels.title: Blocked today
panels.description: Share of today's queries answered from the blocklist.

panels.title: Cached today
panels.description: Share of today's queries answered from Pi-hole's own cache, without asking lancache-dns or Bind9.

panels.title: Gravity domains
panels.description: Domains on the blocklist (gravity), the smaller of the selected instances' counts, so a nebula-sync run that left pihole-02 short shows here. The Gravity domains panel below draws both.

panels.title: Both instances
panels.description: One row per Pi-hole, any probe failing first. The three probe columns are the blackbox dns_lookup (a public name), dns_wildcard (a LAN-domain name, via Bind9) and dns_lancache (a CDN name, via lancache-dns) asked of that instance; Not reporting is a probe seen in the last day and silent now. Serving clients is inferred from the highest query rate among instances passing dns_lookup (see the Summary stat). Click an instance to show only it.

targets.expr: max by (hostname) (label_replace(max by (instance) (probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_lookup", instance=~"pihole-0.*", instance=~"$instance"}) or on (instance) (max by (instance) (last_over_time(probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_lookup", instance=~"pihole-0.*", instance=~"$instance"}[1d])) * 0 - 1), "hostname", "$1", "instance", "(.*)"))

max by (hostname) (label_replace(max by (instance) (probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_wildcard", instance=~"pihole-0.*", instance=~"$instance"}) or on (instance) (max by (instance) (last_over_time(probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_wildcard", instance=~"pihole-0.*", instance=~"$instance"}[1d])) * 0 - 1), "hostname", "$1", "instance", "(.*)"))

max by (hostname) (label_replace(max by (instance) (probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_lancache", instance=~"pihole-0.*", instance=~"$instance"}) or on (instance) (max by (instance) (last_over_time(probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_lancache", instance=~"pihole-0.*", instance=~"$instance"}[1d])) * 0 - 1), "hostname", "$1", "instance", "(.*)"))

max by (hostname) (((pihole_request_rate{hostname=~"$instance"} and on (hostname) label_replace(probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_lookup"} == 1, "hostname", "$1", "instance", "(.*)")) == bool on () group_left () max((pihole_request_rate{job="pihole"} and on (hostname) label_replace(probe_success{job="blackbox", module="dns_lookup"} == 1, "hostname", "$1", "instance", "(.*)")))) or on (hostname) (pihole_request_rate{hostname=~"$instance"} * 0))

panels.title: Probes over time
panels.description: Each Pi-hole probe's result, the VIP's always included. A gap is a probe that was not reporting.

panels.title: Query rate
panels.description: Queries per second into each instance. The VIP holder carries the clients, so a VIP move shows as the two lines swapping.

panels.title: How queries were answered today
panels.description: Today's queries by where the answer came from: Pi-hole's cache, the blocklist, or forwarded to lancache-dns and Bind9. Counts reset at midnight.

panels.title: Blocked share
panels.description: Share of today's queries answered from the blocklist, per instance.

panels.title: Clients and domains today
panels.description: Distinct clients and distinct domains each instance saw today. Clients are LAN addresses, since Pi-hole is the first link of the chain.

panels.title: Query types today
panels.description: Today's queries by record type, across the selected instances.

panels.title: Replies by type today
panels.description: Today's replies by kind, across the selected instances.

panels.title: Top domains today
panels.description: The ten most-queried domains today, summed across the selected instances. Each instance reports only its own top list, so a domain near the bottom of one list and absent from the other is undercounted.

panels.title: Top blocked domains today
panels.description: The ten most-blocked domains today, summed across the selected instances. An instance that has blocked nothing today reports no list.

panels.title: Top clients today, named by NetBox
panels.description: The ten clients that sent the most queries today, summed across the selected instances, each address looked up in NetBox's IP addresses (the hidden client variable holds the same ten). NetBox device or VM is what the address's interface belongs to, NetBox role the device's role (NetBox gives a VM none here), NetBox DNS name and description the address record's own. NetBox reads "not in NetBox" for a client with no address record, usually a DHCP device, which NetBox deliberately does not model; a recorded address assigned to no interface shows blank NetBox device and VM.

panels.title: Forwarded by upstream today
panels.description: Today's forwarded queries per upstream: the lancache-dns pair first, Bind9 when lancache-dns does not answer (strict-order). Upstreams appear by address.

panels.title: Upstream response time
panels.description: Pi-hole's mean response time per upstream. The upstreams are the lancache-dns pair first, then Bind9 when lancache-dns does not answer (strict-order).

panels.title: Gravity domains
panels.description: Domains on each instance's blocklist. The lines must match: pihole-01 owns the lists and nebula-sync copies them to pihole-02 hourly.
